correctness.rationale: The nonunit divisor zeta and Möbius factors are integral and unimodular. The omitted unit term gives a rank-one update, and Möbius inversion on the nonunit index set transforms the matrix to B=D+1u^T with D=diag(d) and u_d=mu(d). Each prime of squarefree n occurs in h=2^(r-1) of those d, so the determinant lemma gives det B=n^(h-1) phi(n). For primes not dividing n, the invertible diagonal plus one rank-one update has nullity at most one. For p dividing n, let T be the h indices divisible by p. The right and left mod-p kernels both vanish off T and are respectively u_T-orthogonal and 1_T-orthogonal hyperplanes. The divided pairing y^T B x/p mod p is well-defined on these kernels; Smith reduction shows its rank counts exactly the p-exponents equal to one. Choose integer lifts supported on T; the rank-one term is divisible by p^2 and the remaining diagonal pairing has units d/p. Its restriction to the two hyperplanes has rank at least h-2. Thus h-2 positive exponents are one and the last is 1+v_p(phi(n)) by the determinant, with h-1 positive exponents total. Combining primes in divisibility order yields the stated Smith diagonal and both corollaries. For a prime modulus n=p the entry is p-1. Independent bounded SymPy Smith spot checks using products of the prime values p-1 or -1, rather than the uploaded incidence code, agreed for n=5187,3298,57,10374. These checks are supplemental; the frozen script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The original theorem's proof is squarefree only; the independently checked instances do not establish the universal formula on their own.

evidence: The indexed broader theorem uses no squarefree hypothesis. For a prime p|n, it takes T=tau(n/p^a) copies of each 1,...,a, removes one 1, and increases one copy of a by v_p(phi(n/p^a)) when positive.
Schlage-Puchta proves the determinant of the full divisor table, not the integral invariant factors of the minor.
broader_coverage.reasoning: At a=1 and r>=2, T=2^(r-1)=h, so the broader theorem leaves h-1 positive p-exponents, of which h-2 are one and the last is 1+v_p(phi(n)), since phi(p)=p-1 is a p-unit. For primes outside n the rule assigns at most a single totient exponent. Left-padding and multiplying these ordered lists gives the exact frozen chain.
